items.title: Blackstone (BX) Stock Looks Fairly Valued Following Its 25% Slide
items.summary: Blackstone has had a tough year in the market, with the stock down 25.4% year to date. That slide puts fresh focus on a basic question for investors: Is the current share price a fair reflection of the returns the asset manager earns on the capital it deploys across real estate, credit, infrastructure and private equity? The 25.4% year to date decline puts real pressure on the idea that Blackstone's current valuation still lines up with the returns it earns on its investment base. Recent...

items.title: Blackstone's crown jewel struggles as real estate woes mount
items.summary: Wall Street’s property powerhouse faces a growing test of its dominance.

items.title: Blackstone (BX), What Is Behind The Fresh Attention Now?
items.summary: Blackstone (BX) is back in focus after Pfizer outlined a funding deal in which the asset manager may provide up to US$1.5b to support development of an experimental obesity drug. Recent moves in Blackstone’s share price show a mixed picture, with the stock down over the year to date and a 1-year total shareholder return of about 12% in decline, yet still logging a gain of roughly 29% over three years and flat performance over five years. items.title: Blackstone Targets $3B Fund to Buy Real Estate Fund Stakes
items.summary: Blackstone seeks $3 billion to buy discounted stakes in real estate funds, targeting data centers, rental housing, and industrial assets.

items.title: Blackstone bets $1.5B on Pfizer’s obesity drug
items.summary: The deal will support a sprawling Phase 3 program for a monthly GLP-1 shot Pfizer acquired by winning a bidding war for the drug’s previous owner, Metsera.

items.title: Blackstone backs Pfizer’s obesity ambitions with $1.5bn fund
items.summary: Pfizer has an extensive clinical programme for berobenatide, acquired via its $10bn takeover of Metsera.

items.title: Blackstone Is Paying Up to $1.5 Billion for Pfizer’s Answer to Wegovy
items.summary: Pfizer just convinced Wall Street's biggest private investor to shoulder its obesity bet, yet the payoff for shareholders may not come from the drug at all. The real story sits in who keeps the upside and what arrives first.
